data.body:
The record-ID check hardcodes the literal prefix `art_v1_` instead of deriving it from `SCHEMA_VERSION`, unlike the new `require_finding_id()` helper added in this same PR (`ai_review_telemetry.py`), which correctly uses `f"arf_v{SCHEMA_VERSION}_"`. All `finding_verdict` records are built via `build_record()`, whose `record_id` prefix always encodes the *current* `SCHEMA_VERSION` at write time. If `SCHEMA_VERSION` is ever bumped, every newly written verdict record will have a `record_id` starting with `art_v2_...`, and this hardcoded check will reject it as `"finding verdict record_id is invalid"`, causing `finding_decisions()` — and therefore both the generation-time catalog load and the publish-time suppression load — to fail outright for any PR with a recorded verdict.

Fix: derive the expected prefix the same way `require_finding_id()` does, e.g. `f"art_v{SCHEMA_VERSION}_"`.
